_comment: ms-2 'Reports panel' (tracking issue #26) — seeds `coord web --fixture`
for the whole milestone's acceptance suite. Schema: coord/dashboard/
fixture.py's module docstring. Per playwright.acceptance.config.ts's
resolveFixturePath, at most ONE *.json file is allowed under this
ms-2/fixtures/ directory — this is it, shared across every ms-2 issue
slice (#21-#25). Authored first by the #21 (RPT-2) test-author; later
slices (#22-#25) extend `report_results` (and, if a report's real
catalogue shape turns out to matter for their own contract section,
`report_catalogue`) rather than adding a second fixture file.
`report_catalogue` is a DELIBERATE OVERRIDE of the real
`coord.reports.catalogue()` (confirmed present in the installed `coord`
CLI as of this writing — code-coordinator#2492/RPT-1 already shipped
upstream) rather than falling back to it. Three reasons, all specific
to what this suite needs to hold still across a WHOLE milestone of
independently-authored slices:
1. contract.md §3b pins an exact SIX-TAB ORDER (drive-queue-status,
issue-activity, completed, decisions, usage, queue-outcomes) that
is NOT the real registry's order (`coord.reports.catalogue()`
iterates `sorted(REPORTS)`, i.e. alphabetically — a different
order). Overriding is the only way to pin the contractual order.
2. contract.md §4b explicitly declines to pin an exact parameter set
per report ('not pinned — no issue body enumerates it'), while
still pinning the choice-→<select> / text-→<input> DISPATCH RULE
as contractual. The real `drive-queue-status` ReportDef today
declares exactly one `text`-kind param (`repo`) and no `choice`-
kind param at all -- which would leave that dispatch rule's
`choice` branch completely unexercised by this milestone's own
report. This fixture's catalogue instead mirrors
mocks/reports-picker.html's/reports-grid.html's own param shape
for drive-queue-status (Repo as `choice`, Search as `text`) so
both branches of the one rule §4b DOES pin are exercised.
3. `report_catalogue_raw`'s doc comment on FixtureServer names exactly
this use case: 'a fixture overrides it only when a test wants a
different catalogue than production's (e.g. a smaller one for a
focused scenario)'.
`title` on every entry is set to this contract's own tab display copy
(§3b's table) directly, sidestepping the question of whether a client
renders `catalogue.title` verbatim or humanizes the key itself --
either implementation choice lands on the same rendered text this way.
`description` text is NOT contractual (§3d: 'this mock's placeholder
copy... only its presence, position and data-testid are contractual') --
the strings below just need to be non-empty and distinct per report so
a tab-switch test can observe the description actually swapping.
`report_results.drive-queue-status` is the one seeded result this
milestone's #21 (RPT-2) slice proves end-to-end -- it mirrors
mocks/reports-grid.html's three rows/eight columns exactly enough to
assert every ColumnMeta.kind this milestone's grid dispatch needs
(text/int/enum/timestamp/duration/list; `money` is exercised by a
later slice's own `completed` row, once added). Timestamps are real
epoch seconds (2026-08-19/20, UTC) so a human diffing this file against
the mock can eyeball the correspondence, but the acceptance spec itself
asserts the timestamp cell's FORMAT SHAPE only (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`), not
an exact clock reading -- contract.md's §6b pins the format, not a
timezone-conversion rule, and this suite has no way to pin the browser
process's local timezone from inside tests/acceptance/ms-NN/**.
Extended by the #22 (RPT-3) test-author: added `report_results` for the
five remaining catalogue reports (issue-activity, completed, decisions,
usage, queue-outcomes) and added a `since`/'Time range' choice param to
issue-activity's/completed's `report_catalogue` entries (mirroring
mocks/reports-row-nav.html's and mocks/reports-completed.html's own
'Time range' select, added on the contract's own 2026-08-20 amendment).
Column shapes for issue-activity/completed/decisions mirror the pinned
MOCKS (reports-row-nav.html/reports-completed.html/reports-decisions.html)
exactly, NOT `coord/reports.py`'s real ISSUE_ACTIVITY_COLUMNS (11) /
DECISIONS_COLUMNS (9) -- contract.md §7.8 explicitly flags that mismatch
as open and unresolved, and this fixture (like drive-queue-status's own
entry above) follows the same established convention of pinning the
MOCK's shape, since `report_catalogue`/`report_results` here already
deliberately overrides the real backend for the whole milestone. Every
identifying/Issue-style column is a single `text`-kind `"api#42"`
string (not split repo/issue columns) so this fixture stays agnostic to
whether a `<Link>` wraps it -- row_identity-aware navigation is RPT-4's
own feature (#23, depends on #22) and this slice's tests deliberately do
not assert either way on that cell's Link-ness, leaving it for #23's own
independent test-author. `completed`'s three rows keep coming from
coord/reports.py's real COMPLETED_COLUMN_META shape (repo+issue already
collapsed to one `issue` field here for the reason above) with one row's
`cost_total: 0.0` specifically to exercise §6b's money-kind zero-renders-
as-em-dash rule. `decisions`' two rows carry `options` as arrays of
`{label, command_or_action, recommended}` dicts -- the exact shape
`coord/reports.py`'s real decision-options builder emits and
`tui/src/app/reports.rs`'s `reports_list_item_text` already consumes --
which is #22's own specifically-named risk (§6d: 'dicts ... not scalars
... render sanely instead of falling through to raw JSON'). `usage` has
no contract mock at all (see contract.md §0's inventory table) so its
shape here is this test-author's own invention purely to prove the tab
is wired into the same generic grid -- see the spec's own TODO comment.
`queue-outcomes`' row/column shape mirrors mocks/reports-chart.html's
grid (below its chart) but `chart` is left `null` here deliberately:
chart rendering is RPT-6's own feature (#25, depends on #22), out of
this slice's scope, and a null `chart` sidesteps any assumption about
how a pre-#25 client handles a populated `chart` key it doesn't render
yet.
